metadata.description: An explicit edge to firebase-server:build-base, NOT `^build`. This entry point cannot compile before the parent's dist exists, so the edge is real -- but it has to be spelled out, because `^build` here would resolve to firebase-server:build, which depends on this very target: a hard cycle. That XOR is the whole design constraint -- either the children get `^build` or the parent aggregates them, never both. Aggregating is the side that keeps one writer per dist directory.  This entry point also imports @dereekb/nestjs/mailgun and @dereekb/util/test, both other families' CHILDREN, so it carries edges to `nestjs:build` and `util:build`. Cross-family deps are spelled as the other family's ROOT `build` (not `build-base`, and not that family's child project): a sibling family's child has no `build` of its own and writes into its parent's dist, so the parent's `build` -- which runs the ESM finalize -- is the only thing that produces a finalized copy for TypeScript to resolve `exports` against. Its one import of @dereekb/firebase-server/test is spec-only (notification.util.spec.ts, zero production use), so it is suppressed with `implicitDependencies: ["!firebase-server-test"]` -- the same suppression `firebase-server` itself already carries. Left in place that false edge serialised this entry point behind `firebase-server-test -> firebase-server-oidc`, pushing it out of wave 1 and making the family's critical path 4 waves instead of 3.
